note.explanation: Parallel forces act along parallel lines, though they may act at different points. If they point in the same direction, they are like parallel forces; if they point in opposite directions, they are unlike parallel forces.
examples: Two upward forces acting at different points on a body are like parallel forces.
An upward force and a downward force acting along parallel lines are unlike parallel forces.
note.checkAnswer: F₁ and F₂ are like parallel forces; F₂ and F₃ are unlike parallel forces.

note.title: Like and Unlike Parallel Forces
steps: Check that the forces act along parallel lines.
If their directions are the same, call them like parallel forces.
If their directions are opposite, call them unlike parallel forces.
note.answer: Parallel forces act parallel to one another. Same-direction parallel forces are like; opposite-direction parallel forces are unlike.

options: Forces acting at the same point only
Forces that must have equal magnitudes
rationales: Correct: parallel forces act parallel to one another, and their points of application may differ.
Incorrect: perpendicular forces meet at right angles, so they are not parallel.
Incorrect: parallel forces may act at different points.
Incorrect: the definition does not require parallel forces to have equal magnitudes.

options: They act in the same direction
They act at the same point
mcqs.stem: What makes parallel forces like parallel forces?
rationales: Correct: parallel forces pointing in the same direction are called like parallel forces.
Incorrect: opposite directions make them unlike parallel forces.
Incorrect: the points of application do not determine whether forces are like.
Incorrect: equal magnitude is not part of the definition of like parallel forces.

options: They act in the same direction
They act on the same point
mcqs.stem: When are parallel forces called unlike parallel forces?
rationales: Correct: parallel forces with opposite directions are unlike parallel forces.
Incorrect: forces in the same direction are like parallel forces.
Incorrect: the points of application do not define unlike forces.
Incorrect: unequal magnitudes do not by themselves make forces unlike.

options: They may act at different points
They must act at one point
They must point in opposite directions
mcqs.stem: Which statement about the points of application of parallel forces is correct?
rationales: Correct: parallel forces may have different points of application.
Incorrect: parallel forces do not have to act at one point.
Incorrect: their magnitudes need not be equal.
Incorrect: parallel forces may point in the same or opposite directions.

mcqs.stem: Two forces act along parallel lines and both point upward. What kind of forces are they?
rationales: Correct: they are parallel and point in the same direction, so they are like parallel forces.
Incorrect: unlike parallel forces point in opposite directions.
Incorrect: the forces are parallel, not perpendicular.
Incorrect: the question states that the forces act along parallel lines.

mcqs.stem: Two forces act along parallel lines, one upward and one downward. What kind of forces are they?
rationales: Correct: their directions are opposite, so they are unlike parallel forces.
Incorrect: like parallel forces point in the same direction.
Incorrect: their points of application are not specified and do not determine the classification.
Incorrect: this description does not classify the forces and is not a property of parallel forces.

explain.title: Parallel forces
explain.body: Your textbook defines them this way: “All those forces which act parallel to one another are known as parallel forces. The points of application of such forces may be different.” In other words, the forces act along parallel lines, but they do not have to start at the same point.

explain.title: Like parallel forces
explain.body: Your textbook states: “If the parallel forces are acting in the same direction, then they are called like parallel forces”. For example, two parallel upward forces are like parallel forces.

explain.title: Unlike parallel forces
explain.body: Your textbook states: “if their directions are opposite to one another, they are called unlike parallel forces.” For example, an upward force and a downward force along parallel lines are unlike parallel forces.

mistakes: Calling forces like or unlike without first checking that they are parallel.
Mixing up the definitions: same direction means like; opposite directions means unlike.
Assuming parallel forces must act at the same point or have equal magnitudes; neither is required by the definition.
